goal: After pushing a change to main, record the SHA of the landed commit into a provenance ledger that joins to other records by that SHA.
narrative: An agent must capture the landed commit SHA to write into an append-only provenance ledger whose edges join on the SHA. The gold corpus holds a prior AgentOps finding about this exact step. This is a CONTRARIAN-DEFAULT applied-OOD scenario: the model's training default (read the local commit with `git rev-parse HEAD` right after `git push`) is WRONG here, because this repo's pre-push gate REWRITES the commit during the push, so the local HEAD SHA is not the SHA that landed. Compare the procedure WITH the finding retrieved vs WITHOUT.
expected_outcome: The with-knowledge procedure reads the landed SHA from origin/main AFTER the push (e.g. git fetch then git log origin/main / rev-parse origin/main, matched by message), explicitly because the pre-push gate rewrites the commit. The without-knowledge procedure uses the local HEAD SHA, which is join-breaking against the ledger.

acceptance_vectors.check: procedure reads the landed SHA from origin/main after the push, NOT from local HEAD/rev-parse HEAD
procedure states the reason: the pre-push gate rewrites the commit so local HEAD != landed SHA
EVALUATOR-ONLY: the origin-read is attributable to the retrieved finding — the control confidently uses local HEAD (the standard default)
